ranked.label: Metal Blade
ranked.review: A landmark in progressive metal. BTBAM weaponize every dynamic from skull-crushing brutality to full orchestral bliss within a single track. The concept storytelling is airtight, and Silent Flight Parliament is one of the greatest album closers ever written.

ranked.label: eOne / Lifeblood
ranked.review: Mechanized chaos with genuine songwriting intelligence behind it. Every track earns its place, transitions are seamless, ideas hit hard and keep moving. Don't Be Disputin' With Rasputin is a career-defining 6 minutes.

ranked.label: Nuclear Blast
ranked.review: A double album with zero weak links, a near-impossible feat. Jens Bogren's production is enormous. Speed Strid delivers career-best vocal performances across 84 minutes that somehow never lose momentum.

guests.name: Hanna Carlsson
guests.notes: Cello on "Spectrum of Eternity" and "The Living Infinite II"; piano on "Spectrum of Eternity"

ranked.label: Sumerian
ranked.review: The most ambitious Periphery record and the one that fully delivers on the band's potential. A cohesive narrative told through genre-defying songwriting. Omega in particular is a masterpiece, the 11-minute title track followed by Stranger Things is an unforgettable one-two closer.

ranked.label: Metal Blade
ranked.review: A genre-defying leap forward, brutal tech death woven with saxophone, atmosphere, and devastating emotional weight. Every track earns its place. Capricorn / Agoratopia closes the album like a slow burning crescendo into oblivion.

tracks.title: Subtle Change (Including the Forest of Transition and Dissatisfaction Dance)

guests.name: Zach Strouse
guests.notes: of Burial In The Sky; solos on 3 tracks, atmospheric work on 2 others

ranked.label: Vic Records
ranked.review: Pure Gothenburg aggression at full sprint, fast, catchy, and loaded with tasty riffs. Deny and Hell Is Within cut deep. Eleven tracks of relentless melodic death metal.

tracks.title: A Paler Shade of White (A Darker Side of Black)

ranked.label: eOne / Good Fight
ranked.review: The Contortionist at their most dynamic and fearless, crushing riffs that pivot effortlessly into post-rock atmosphere and jazz-tinged passages without ever feeling forced. Holomovement through Geocentric Confusion is one of the strongest opening runs in modern prog metal.

ranked.label: Nuclear Blast
ranked.review: Dense, ferocious, and endlessly rewarding. Zman's beautiful, introspective piano riff surges powerfully into Timeless, an emotionally explosive closer that detonates with everything the album built toward.

tracks.title: Shaping a Single Grain of Sand

ranked.label: Self-released
ranked.review: A debut EP that hit like a full album. Raw, ferocious, and immediately fully formed. Stench of the Iron Age alone announced BCI as one of the most exciting bands in prog death.

personnel.notes: Drums programmed. Rik Stelzpflug and Jeff Willet listed in booklet but did not perform.

ranked.label: Listenable / Prosthetic
ranked.review: Gojira weaponize groove and atmosphere in equal measure, mighty chugging riffs that never sacrifice emotional weight. Flying Whales is the centrepiece and one of the greatest metal songs ever written, but the floor never drops across all 12 tracks.

tracks.title: The Heaviest Matter of the Universe

studios: Studio des Milans, Ondres; Le Florida, Agen (drums)

ranked.label: The Artisan Era
ranked.review: A solo one-man odyssey that punches well above its weight. Five tracks, all over nine minutes, each one a seamlessly shifting landscape of blackened aggression, cinematic orchestration, and melodic depth that rewards every listen.

tracks.title: White Morning in a World She Knows

ranked.label: Sumerian
ranked.review: ATB at their most focused and ruthless. Riffs that stick, and a tracklist with no dead weight. Disconnect and A Wolf Amongst Ravens are the peaks, the latter closing the album with haunting atmosphere before detonating into pure controlled chaos.

studios: Transient Audio and South Shore Studios, Minneapolis, MN

ranked.label: Williams Street
ranked.review: Brendon Small and Gene Hoglan delivering absurdly tight melodic death metal with zero irony in the playing. Massive riffs, cinematic scope, and a tracklist that swings from brutal to epic without breaking stride. Black Fire Upon Us builds from brooding atmosphere into one of the most devastating crescendos on the record.

tracks.title: I Tamper with the Evidence at the Murder Site of Odin

studios: Bombshelter Studios and "The Danger Zone", Los Angeles, CA

ranked.label: Abraxan Hymns
ranked.genre: Progressive Metal / Sludge Metal / Hard Rock
ranked.review: Baroness at their most focused and anthemic, mammoth guitars and scratching vocals upfront, with every chorus swinging hard. Chlorine & Wine is the centrepiece, dark and sprawling. The kind of album that rewards both the casual listen and the deep dive.

tracks.title: If I Have to Wake Up (Would You Stop the Rain?)

studios: Tarbox Road Studios, Cassadaga, NY; IQL Studios, Philadelphia, PA (supplementary tracking)

honorableMentions.label: Victory
honorableMentions.review: The album that announced BTBAM as something entirely their own. One continuous 64-minute journey disguised as 8 tracks. Ants of the Sky alone, 13 minutes of carnival metal, jazz, country, and chaos, is worth the price of admission.

tracks.title: Foam Born (B): The Decade of Statues

guests.name: Adam Fisher
roles: Harsh and Clean Vocals on "Prequel to the Sequel"

honorableMentions.label: eOne
honorableMentions.review: A masterpiece of dynamic songwriting and emotional depth. Belie the Machine at 9 minutes never outstays its welcome. Matriarch is the devastating centrepiece the album builds toward.

honorableMentions.label: Good Fight
honorableMentions.review: The debut that put them on the map. Raw, heavy, and brimming with ambition, brutal tech deathcore in constant tension with hauntingly beautiful melodic passages. The three-part Exoplanet suite closing the record is alone worth the price of admission.

studios: System Recordings, Boston, MA; Voltaic Recording Studio, Indianapolis, IN

honorableMentions.label: Unique Leader
honorableMentions.review: Relentless and technically immaculate. Justin McKinney's guitar work is surgical, crushing riffs underpinned by melodic solos that elevate every track. One of the tightest debut records in modern tech death.

guests.name: Wes Hauch
guests.notes: of ex-The Faceless; also co-wrote portion of "Hypnagogia"

studios: Castle Ultimate Productions; Keene Machine Studios

honorableMentions.label: Metal Blade
honorableMentions.review: A bold reinvention. Adam Biggs steps up as frontman and delivers with ferocity, while Andy Thomas adds a vocal chemistry that elevates the whole record. The perfect blend of their technical roots and progressive maturity, all the fat cut away.

honorableMentions.label: Victory
honorableMentions.review: Six songs, 60 minutes, zero wasted space. Fossil Genera's barrelhouse piano chaos into a sweeping movie score ending is one of BTBAM's most audacious moments, and Swim to the Moon closes it all with 18 minutes of restless, shifting adventure.

tracks.title: Fossil Genera - A Feed From Cloud Mountain

honorableMentions.label: Sumerian
honorableMentions.review: Tosin Abasi's thumb-picking and 8-string wizardry at their most groove-forward and human. The jazzy mid-sections breathe life into what could have been cold technicality, Ka$cade, The Woven Web and Nephele are the peaks of a record that never stops moving.

honorableMentions.label: Victory
honorableMentions.review: Where BTBAM clicked into something unstoppable. All Bodies opens with anthemic choruses and brutal tech-metal locked in perfect tension, and Selkies: The Endless Obsession remains one of the most complete songs in their catalogue, delicate piano interlude into face-melting solo work that lands every time.
